cases.name: durable-plan-written-to-disk

graders.name: result
graders.graderMarkdown:
The user is about to start multi-day, multi-crate work on revmc and has said plainly that a previous session lost everything when its context filled up: he had to re-explain the background from scratch, and an approach he had already ruled out got retried. Unlike the read-only sibling case, this run could write files, and the working directory is the repo root.

Judge the files on disk, not the reply. Grade one thing: could a session that opens tomorrow with no memory of this conversation pick the work up from these files alone?

PASS requires all three:

- The work is broken into steps on disk, and a status record covers those steps saying where each stands and what the next action is.
- The saved text carries the background a cold reader would otherwise have to ask him for: what revmc is and what EOF support means here, the entry point or crates the work touches, and that the legacy path must not regress.
- Ruled-out approaches have a durable home, so a dead end gets written down rather than retried. Nothing has been ruled out on this work yet, so a named place for them is enough and an empty one is not a miss.

FAIL if any of the three is missing, if the files hold only his own four steps copied back under a bare title, or if the substance lives in the reply while the files are stubs or placeholders promising content that was never written.

Judge substance only. How many files, what they are named, whether they live in `.planning/` or elsewhere, section layout, ordering, length, and language all do not matter.
